subject.title: [Feature]: Support configurable request labels for Gemini API calls (GCP billing tracking)

question: Should OpenClaw expose static request labels for Google Vertex model calls, and what public config shape and validation policy should own that contract?
rationale: Adding request labels creates a new provider config surface with billing, privacy, and cardinality implications that the repository policy treats as a maintainer product/config decision.

options.title: Approve Vertex-only static labels
options.body: Add a Google-plugin-owned `google-vertex` label config with strict GCP label validation, low-cardinality guidance, docs, tests, and live proof.

options.title: Defer to broader attribution policy
options.body: Keep this open while maintainers design a cross-provider attribution surface instead of adding a Google-specific key now.

options.title: Reject OpenClaw config surface
options.body: Tell operators to handle billing labels outside OpenClaw, accepting a weaker self-hosted operator story.

recommendation.title: Approve Vertex-only static labels
recommendation.body: Add a Google-plugin-owned `google-vertex` label config with strict GCP label validation, low-cardinality guidance, docs, tests, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current-history signal across the Google transport and config schema surfaces where the product/config decision would land.
